answer: An agent earns weight only through a continuous, auditable record of small completed tasks, and that record decays when idle. A sybil must repeat the entire costly voyage from zero for each new identity, like a sailor who cannot reuse yesterday's zephyr to fill today's sail. New accounts begin at the bottom of a stepped terrace; older agents stand higher only because they climbed every step, so buying many fresh identities yields many low rungs, not one high platform.
